title: Rhythm Nation
location: Te Wharekura and Te Wānanga, 117 Quay Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Join us for a vibrant, interactive performance celebrating Māori music and movement as part of NZ Music Month.
Led by Te Whare Karioi, from the heart of Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei, each performer descends from the eponymous ancestor, Tuperiri.
These free hour-long sessions will showcase taonga pūkaea, pūtatara, taiaha, poi and haka, with opportunities to participate and learn about the cultural significance behind each art form.
This free, whānau-friendly event invites you to connect with Tāmaki Makaurau’s rich whakapapa through live performance and hands-on experiences.
Feel the pulse of the haka, hear the call of ancient instruments and move to the rhythm of poi.

title: Meaningful Connections Meetup
description:

title: Welcome to the next AWS Auckland Well-Architected Meetup for 2026!

At each meetup, we focus on learning and networking in a friendly and inclusive atmosphere and explore best-practices in AWS. This has resulted in the AWS Well-Architected Meetups becoming the most popular AWS Meetups in ANZ 🥳

**Please also note that AWS Security now requests a company name and company email where it is available. If you are a student, please list your institution and your student email address at that institution 👍**

* **Yadwinder Sharma, Founder, https://www.nimbal.ai**

**From 5 Days to 5 Minutes: Reimagining Well-Architected QA with Autonomous AI**

Modern software delivery is accelerating faster than traditional QA can keep up. Teams are facing rising costs, delayed releases and significant reputational risks when quality is compromised. At the same time, AI-generated code and rapid release cycles are outpacing manual testing capabilities.

This session explores how autonomous, cloud-native QA powered by AI agents is transforming software verification—reducing testing time from days to minutes and costs from thousands to tens of dollars, supported by AWS Well-Architected principles of:

Operational Excellence: Automating QA workflows with self-service, zero-setup AI agents
Reliability: Detecting broken links, errors and performance issues before production
Cost Optimization: Moving from high fixed QA costs to on-demand, per-run pricing models and more

title: Run Better AI Coding Agents for $0 — Straight From Your Own Laptop
description:
Looking for a chill but productive space to code, learn, and connect with other developers? Whether you’re just starting out or deep into a side project, you’re welcome here.

🚨 **Special Feature This Week: Local Coding Agents** This week features a hands-on walkthrough by **[Eugene Oskin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eugene-oskin/)**, who will be showing us how to set up local LLMs on a MacBook to run coding agents that hit Sonnet 4.5 levels of performance.
He’ll be breaking down his exact stack:

* **The Software:** Configuring LM Studio (Developer mode) and setting up local REST API endpoints.
* **The Hardware:** Pushing an Apple M4 Max with 64GB RAM to dedicate over 51GB of VRAM for model acceleration.
* **The Models:** Live demos of loading and running **Qwen3.6-27b** alongside the highly efficient **Nvidia Nemotron models family**.

Alongside the demo, this remains a casual, community-driven space where you can:

* 💻 Work on your own coding projects
* 🎯 Share goals or progress (totally optional!)
* 🎙️ Talk tech and discuss local AI setups
* ☕ Meet like-minded people over coffee

Come with your laptop, your curiosity, or just a love for tech. Stay for the connections and good vibes.
☕ *This event is hosted at a local café, so we kindly ask that you support the venue by purchasing a drink or snack if you can.*
No pressure, no strict schedule—just code, coffee, AI, and vibes.

title: World Product Day 2026 - How do we really AI?
description:
We're celebrating [World Product Day 2026](https://www.worldproductday.com/) by getting beyond the hype to hear 4 product people tell us how they are really using AI in their day to day work!

* **Rahul:** Discovery, Rewired: From Transcripts to Production with AI - the story of how Global Dairy Trade took an idea from interviews to the real world
* **Peony:** A product team of one - how a solo PM uses AI to operate in the goldilocks zone, just enough process, just enough output, moving fast enough to learn and find PMF
* **Darren:** Product discovery with agents - from strategy to roadmaps
* **Emilie:** AI in product design - allowing the designer to focus on the human tasks

The event will start with **networking at 5.30pm**, followed by the **talk from 6pm!**

**About our speakers:**
**Rahul Singh** [https://www.linkedin.com/in/rahulsinghnz/](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rahulsinghnz/)

Outside the day job, Rahul runs AI PM Briefing, a weekly briefing for product managers on what's actually shipping in AI (tools, patterns, case studies), and is the author of ‘Don't Think, Change‘- a field guide to behaviour change for product teams.

**Peony Pangputt** [https://www.linkedin.com/in/peonypangputt/](https://www.linkedin.com/in/peonypangputt/)
Product Manager at FileInvite, a B2B SaaS platform helping US commercial lenders automate the collection of loan information faster. title: Auckland Youth Symphonic Band
location: Avondale Library, 93 Rosebank Road, Avondale, Auckland, Auckland
description:
The Auckland Youth Symphonic Band (AYSB) is Auckland's only community youth concert band based in central Auckland.
Conducted by Michael Jamieson, the band aims to give young musicians (from year seven to university age) opportunities to play with other musical students from across Auckland - especially when players may not have the chance to play in musical ensembles at their schools.
The AYSB regularly performs in collaboration with the Auckland Wind Orchestra. Over the last few years they have played for the Glenbrook Vintage Railway and the NZ Yorkshire Society. They have achieved Silver awards at the New Zealand National Concert Band Festival (2019, 2021, 2023), as well as a Gold award in the NZCBA Festival (2022).
Come and join them at Avondale Library as they showcase their incredible talent in a live performance.

description:
You’ve heard the whispers. You’ve seen the chaos. Now *Stamptown* is coming out in the daylight… with a few secrets up its sleeves.
Hosted by the naughty boy of clown Zach Zucker, this is a high-energy, anything-could-happen variety spectacular - packed with big laughs, bold surprises, and the kind of anarchic showmanship that makes kids go “WHAT?!” and adults go “WAIT… was that for me?” (Yes. Yes it was.)
Think: the Stamptown spirit you’d expect but remixed for families. It’s all the wow, silliness and theatrical mayhem, with the edges safely rounded. The kids get the visual gags and wild moments. The grown-ups get the sly little layers. Like a Disney movie… if Disney had a slightly unhinged cousin who runs a circus.
Come as a family. Leave with in-jokes. And the burning need to tell everyone you know: “I can’t explain it - you just have to go.”
Presented by the NZ Comedy Trust as part of the NZ International Comedy Festival with Best Foods Mayo.

**AI Landing Zones**
As organisations rapidly adopt AI, many struggle to move beyond isolated proofs of concept into secure, scalable, and governed production environments. This session explores how AI Landing Zones provide the foundational platform needed to operationalise AI safely and sustainably at enterprise scale.

**Chanaka Nissanka** is a Principal Consultant based in Auckland, with extensive experience helping large enterprises design and adopt cloud platforms at scale. He specialises in Azure Landing Zones, cloud governance, and operating model design, working closely with architects, security teams, and business stakeholders to enable secure, scalable cloud and AI adoption. Chanaka has led and advised on complex transformation initiatives across regulated and high‑consumption environments, bridging strategy and hands‑on implementation.

title: 📌Lake Rototoa
description:
On Sunday, the 17th of May, we will embark on a hike that encircles Lake Rototoa and the surrounding reserve. Lake Rototoa is about 30km north of Helensville, and adjoins Te Rau Puriri regional park. The rough track that runs alongside the lake on the south western side is quite overgrown and features numerous windfalls that require climbing over. On the western side, there is no established path, necessitating careful navigation and preparation for challenging terrain in certain areas. On the northeastern side there is farm land to cross. The hike covers a distance of approximately 10 kilometers and features undulating terrain.

The predominant vegetation consists of Manuka and Kanuka, and on the western side boasts one of the largest remnants of native broadleaf species in the South Kaipara heads region. Lake Rototoa is recognized as the cleanest, largest, and deepest of all the ancient sand dune lakes located in the Woodhill Forest area. It is occasionally referred to as "Ototoa," although this is a misspelling of Rototoa.
